# answerui


<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

Use the `@answerdotai/answerui` npm package for the browser foundation:
a stylesheet keyed on semantic HTML attributes and CSS custom
properties, optional fonts, and vanilla JavaScript modules. Use the
`answerui-py` Python package to add [FastHTML](https://fastht.ml)
constructors and a registry for app-specific CSS and browser behavior on
top of those same assets.

Python constructors emit marked HTML, such as `<section card>` from
`Card()` and `<button btn>` from `Btn()`. AnswerUI does not restyle
unmarked form elements. Frontend frameworks such as Svelte can emit the
same markup and import the JavaScript modules directly without Python.
The notebooks cover the generated OKLCH palette, typography and spacing
scales, parent-driven layouts, UI components, and the Python registry.

Read `answerui.skill` with `doc(answerui.skill)` for an LLM guide to
building FastHTML pages, inspecting and customising registered
components, and previewing results in a persistent Python kernel.

## Install

For a JavaScript app:

``` sh
npm install @answerdotai/answerui
```

Import the stylesheet once:

``` js
import '@answerdotai/answerui/styles.css';
import {mountPopover} from '@answerdotai/answerui/floating.js';
```

`@answerdotai/answerui/styles.css` works without JavaScript, including
native dialogs, disclosures, and CSS tooltips. Import individual browser
modules only for components that require JavaScript:
`@answerdotai/answerui/floating.js` for popovers,
`@answerdotai/answerui/fit.js` for responsive navbars,
`@answerdotai/answerui/interactions.js` for tabs, toolbars, and hover
cards, and `@answerdotai/answerui/copy.js` for clipboard actions. Load
`@answerdotai/answerui/fonts.css` to use the bundled IBM Plex font
faces.

For server-rendered or static HTML,
`import '@answerdotai/answerui/browser.js'` mounts those behaviors
automatically on marked elements and observes later DOM insertions. In
Svelte or another component framework, import the individual modules
inside your component lifecycle instead of loading
`@answerdotai/answerui/browser.js`.

For FastHTML:

``` sh
pip install answerui-py
```

If you serve the browser assets directly from Python,
`from answerui import assets` returns the packaged `Path` to the assets
directory.

## Use from Python

`reg.hdrs()` returns the shared foundation stylesheet, browser scripts,
and registered app rules. `reg.ftrs()` returns the `fastlucide` icon
sprite sheet. Because FastHTML evaluates both on every response, newly
registered rules take effect on the next request without a restart:

``` python
from fasthtml.common import *
from answerui.all import *
```

``` python
app = FastHTML(hdrs=reg.hdrs(), ftrs=reg.ftrs())
rt = app.route
```

To serve cached assets instead of inlining them on every page, create
the app without `reg.hdrs()` or `reg.ftrs()`, then call
`reg.serve(app)`. That call registers the headers, icon sprite sheet,
and content-hashed asset routes while preserving relative imports
between the browser JavaScript modules.

``` python
served_app = FastHTML()
reg.serve(served_app);
```

Each Python constructor renders standard HTML with a semantic attribute.
Below, `Card` renders `<section card>` and `Stack` wraps the children in
`<div stack>` to space them vertically:

``` python
page = Card(Stack(H2('Profile'), Field('Name', Input(name='name')), Cluster(Btn('Save'), Btn('Cancel', variant='secondary'))))
demo(page)
```

``` html
<section card>
  <div stack>
    <h2>Profile</h2>
    <div field>
<label for="_ltza-XI9Ree3DkK7W96AMg">Name</label>      <div field-control>
        <input input name="name" id="_ltza-XI9Ree3DkK7W96AMg">
      </div>
    </div>
    <div cluster>
<button type="button" btn btn-variant="primary">Save</button><button type="button" btn btn-variant="secondary">Cancel</button>    </div>
  </div>
</section>
```

`demo(page)` renders the Python markup with the same stylesheet and
browser scripts used by JavaScript applications.

## Customise

Register standard CSS at the scope you want to change: `:root` custom
properties via `reg.rule` for the whole app, a scoped selector for one
region, or a component rule via `Btn.rule`. Because registered rules are
placed in the `app` cascade layer after every framework layer except
`utilities`, they override AnswerUI defaults without modifying the
package:

``` python
reg.rule(':root { --hue: 150; --radius: 0; }', 'theme')
Btn.rule('caps', 'text-transform: uppercase;')
```

    Btn.caps [app] [btn]

Call `.variant()` on a component to declare a named style modifier. The
component constructor then accepts that variant name as a keyword
argument. Declared variants also appear in the component’s
documentation:

``` python
Btn.variant('cta', '--ui-pad-block: var(--space); --ui-pad-inline: var(--space2); font-size: var(--text1);', doc='The landing page call to action.')
```

    Btn.cta [app] :is([btn])[cta]: The landing page call to action.

Declaring a variant registers an `app`-layer rule for that attribute on
the component element without modifying the default styles in
`styles.css`.

``` python
demo(Btn('Request access', cta=True))
```

``` html
<button type="button" btn btn-variant="primary" cta>Request access</button>
```

``` python
Btn
```

### `Btn(*c, variant='primary', size=None, href=None, type='button', icon=False, **attrs)`

A raised action, latched by aria-pressed and sunken while busy or
expanded

Root selector: `[btn]`.

Declared variants: - `cta`: The landing page call to action.

Rules: - `base` (app) - `caps` (app)

## Previews in notebooks

`demo(page)` returns a `Preview` with two MIME representations: an HTML
iframe containing the full stylesheet and browser scripts, and a
Markdown block of the HTML markup. Because each iframe embeds the entire
stylesheet, committing them would bloat notebooks and churn diffs on
every stylesheet edit. `Preview._repr_mimebundle_` sets nbdev’s `strip`
metadata flag on the HTML output. When you run `nbdev-clean`, it strips
the iframe and keeps the Markdown markup in git. In a fresh clone, run
the notebook cells to display the iframes again.

For the docs, set `exec_all` in `pyproject.toml`:

``` toml
[tool.nbdev]
exec_all = true
```

`nbdev-docs` then executes every notebook and renders each iframe from
the current code.

## With an LLM

`answerui.skill` is a [pyskill](https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/pyskills)
whose module docstring documents how to use AnswerUI in a Python kernel.
Run `list_pyskills()` to discover it, `doc(answerui.skill)` to read the
guide, and `doc(Btn)` to inspect a component’s signature, declared
variants, and CSS rules.
